location: Syncrude Aurora North Mine, Alberta, Canada
fatal_blocker: The public research literature identifies 10, 20 and 30 cm treatment depths and a randomized layout of thirty-six one-hectare cells, but repeatedly relies on a private 2017 O'Kane Consultants monitoring/construction report for cover-design details. That report was not found in a publicly retrievable form. The accessible papers do not publish final measured as-built thickness values, numerical thickness uncertainty, construction survey accuracy, or a coordinate table/GIS deliverable linking exact measured depths to cell polygons. The treatment matrix also changes coversoil material, subsoil configuration and planting treatments, so a depth-only matched pair is not established from the public record.
key_evidence: The study comprises twelve alternate one-hectare cover designs replicated three times for thirty-six cells.
Accessible papers describe 10, 20 and 30 cm coversoil depths using peat-mineral or forest-floor mineral materials.
The randomized cells also vary underlying subsoil material and arrangement and were planted with multiple tree species and densities.
The public HESS paper cites OKC 2017 for treatment layout and construction/performance details.
No publicly retrievable copy of the cited 2017 OKC report or equivalent final construction certification was found.
No accessible public document publishes final measured thicknesses, numerical depth uncertainty or survey-controlled measured-depth polygons.

sources.hess_2020: Characterizing uncertainty in the hydraulic parameters of oil sands mine reclamation covers and its influence on water balance predictions
sources.canadian_journal_soil_science_2017: Carbon, nitrogen and phosphorus release from peat and forest floor-based cover soils used during oil sands reclamation

next_action: Continue the approved search for a publicly retrievable final construction survey that assigns measured depths and uncertainty to large georeferenced vegetated polygons.
